entities.summary:
Jean-Baptiste Budes, Comte de Guébriant, a distinguished Marshal of France, emerged as a pivotal military commander during the tumultuous final decade of the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648). Born in 1602 in Saint-Carreuc, Brittany, Guébriant's career was inextricably linked to Cardinal Richelieu's ambitious policy of asserting French dominance against the Habsburgs. His strategic acumen and battlefield prowess were instrumental in shifting the military balance in Central Europe, particularly through his campaigns in Germany, which paved the way for France's future territorial gains and cemented its status as a continental power in the mid-17th century.

Guébriant's military career reached its zenith with a series of crucial victories. After distinguishing himself in various campaigns, including the relief of Casale (1629) and the capture of Trèves (1635), he was entrusted with commanding French forces in Germany. His decisive triumph at the Battle of Kempen in January 1642, where his Franco-Weimarian army routed an Imperial force led by General Guillaume de Lamboy, was a strategic masterpiece that secured the Lower Rhine region for France. This victory was followed by the capture of several key fortresses and further successful maneuvers against Bavarian and Imperial forces, showcasing his tactical brilliance and aggressive operational style. He was elevated to Marshal of France in 1642, a testament to his indispensable role.
